sources.read: checked-in schema.json (the live admin API was not read: no admin token here)

kinds.question: Must every one have one, or can it stand alone? Could it ever be attached to several at once, now or later (then it is 'is-on', and changing your mind after real data exists is a migration)? Can it move to another later? When the one it belongs to goes, does this go with it, stay orphaned, or block the removal?
kinds.distinguishes: one target, no details on the link itself; read the other way it is 'has many' (the same edge)
kinds.projectsTo: Link (Pointer) with required/optional and an on-delete rule; the reverse read is a query, not a column

kinds.sentence: a {from} is on a {to} for a while, with details of its own
kinds.question: Can it be on two at once? Does it start and end (dates, active)? What stays and what goes when it ends? Which details belong to the link and not to either end (a role, a type, a position)?
kinds.distinguishes: a junction record that carries details; a plain pairing with none is 'together'
kinds.projectsTo: a collection of its own with two Links and the details as fields; never a Links (Relation) column, which cannot hold a date

kinds.question: Does the pairing ever need a date, a reason, a role or an order? (Then it is 'is-on'.) Can the same pair be listed twice?
kinds.projectsTo: Links (Relation) or a junction collection; the unique pair rule

kinds.sentence: a {from}'s {field} is one of a fixed list
kinds.question: Who may add to the list, and does adding need a developer? Is the list the same for everyone? Does a value ever retire (then it is a lifecycle, not a choice)? Will you ever need details about a list entry (then it is a collection)?
kinds.distinguishes: a value from a declared list on the record itself, not a link to a record
kinds.projectsTo: Choice (String + oneOf rule); the mutant is free text where a list belongs

kinds.sentence: a {from} carries a list of {to} on itself
kinds.question: Will you ever ask it the other way round ('which {from}s name this one')? Will the list grow to dozens? Will the list need details per entry? If any, each entry is its own link — a parent carrying dozens of list entries is the query that falls apart.
kinds.distinguishes: ids or values stored as an array column, no record per entry
kinds.projectsTo: List (Array); the mutant is a list of ids that nobody can query from the other side

kinds.question: How deep can it go? Can a thing be moved under another? Can it be its own ancestor? Does a child inherit anything from its parent?
kinds.distinguishes: a link from a collection to itself
kinds.projectsTo: a Link to the same collection; the path operation walks it (ONT-004)

kinds.sentence: a {from} also exists in another system, known there by its own id
kinds.question: Can it exist here before it exists there, or there before here — and what is silently skipped when it does? Which side wins when they disagree? What is it called over there? What happens over there when it ends here?
kinds.distinguishes: an id or a provenance record naming another system, not a record in this one
kinds.projectsTo: a Text field per system, unique, plus a sync log; the enrolment note is this kind's unasked question

kinds.sentence: two {from}s turned out to be one thing
kinds.question: How do you tell? Who decides when the system is not sure? Which record survives and which fields win? Can a merge be undone?
kinds.distinguishes: a link between records of the same collection that means identity, not hierarchy
kinds.projectsTo: a 'superseded by' Link on the same collection plus a match record; never a delete

kinds.sentence: a {from} can end without being deleted
kinds.question: When it ends, what stays and what goes — its record, its history, the things on it, its access elsewhere, the lists it is on? Can it come back, and does coming back make a new one or revive the old? Who may end it? When it ends, is a note or a reason written with it — which detail, and must it be there?
kinds.distinguishes: a status, an active flag, an end date, an archive or erasure record — the record is kept
kinds.projectsTo: a status Choice or a Date, a rule for each linked thing, and a 'delete: nobody' permission; the archive note is this kind's unasked question

kinds.sentence: something happened to a {from} at a time, and the record of it is kept
kinds.question: Is it kept forever? Can it be undone, and does undoing make a new record or remove this one? Who did it, and who may see the history? Does the thing it happened to need it to exist?
kinds.distinguishes: a record that is an event about another record (a log, an action, an attendance, a submission, a read receipt)
kinds.projectsTo: a collection with a Link, a Date and a 'who' Link; update and delete: nobody

kinds.sentence: a {from} is seen and changed by whoever it belongs to, and by nobody else unless said
kinds.question: Who else may see it — a role, an admin of the thing it sits on, everyone? Does ownership follow a path (the holder of the account the person is on)? What happens to it when its owner ends?
kinds.distinguishes: a rule about visibility, not a fact about the world: creator-owns, an access list, a tenant, an admin link
kinds.projectsTo: the security file's permissions and creatorOwns; a path-shaped rule needs ONT-004

kinds.sentence: a {from} is extra detail about one {to}, at most one each
kinds.question: Is there ever more than one? Does it exist without the thing it extends? Is it computed (then nobody edits it) or written by a person? Which of its fields will you filter or sort the main thing by — those stay on the main thing, or every such query goes through the extension and you end up copying the field back by hand.
kinds.distinguishes: a one-to-one link, usually unique or the record's own key
kinds.projectsTo: a Link with a unique rule; or fields on the thing itself when it is small

kinds.sentence: a {from} names its {to} by something a person could retype (an email, a code)
kinds.question: What if it is misspelled, or changes, or two things share it? Should it be a link instead?
kinds.distinguishes: a natural key stored as text where a Link would be
kinds.projectsTo: a Link; the mutant is the text itself

kinds.sentence: a {from} points at one thing that may be any of several kinds, and says which
kinds.question: Which kinds can it point at, exactly? What happens when the thing it points at goes? Can it be re-pointed?
kinds.distinguishes: an id beside a kind field; no single target collection
kinds.projectsTo: a kind Choice plus a Text id; the mutant is an id with no kind beside it

kinds.sentence: a {from} is agreed at some point, and after that it stays as it was agreed
kinds.question: Who agrees it, and what is it called when they do (issued, sent, sealed, published)? After that, which of its details may still change? To put a mistake right, is it withdrawn, or replaced by a new one that says which it replaces? May a draft be thrown away, and may an agreed one ever be deleted?
kinds.distinguishes: a draft that becomes agreed (issued, sent, sealed, published) and is then frozen while still in force; 'ends' keeps a record that stopped, 'happened-to' was never editable
kinds.projectsTo: a status Choice (draft / agreed / withdrawn), an agreed-at Date and an 'amends' Link to itself; the moves and the freeze kept inside the write (onlyWhile), and no deleting an agreed one if said

evidence.note: a new attempt is a new record and the old one stays (unique with learner, concept and section): amend by a new record
draft / issued / withdrawn, Frappe's draft / submitted / cancelled under other words
a new attempt is a new record and the old one stays: amend by a new record
a draft kept beside the version that was published
sealed until a day; sealEnvelope refuses a day that is not still to come

notes.note: the archive note (what stays, what ends when a person is archived)
notes.question: When a person stops, what stays and what goes — their record and its history, the account they are on, their access to the things elsewhere, the lists they are on? Can they come back, and is that the old record revived or a new one?

notes.note: the enrolment note (enrolment elsewhere silently skipped)
notes.question: Can a person be added here before they exist over there — and if they can, what is silently skipped, and how would anyone notice?

notes.note: the incident report (a paying member invisible for an unknown period; the remediation that made a person without the links)
notes.question: What must be linked for a thing to count as what you call it — is a person with no link to an account a member, or just a contact? When something arrives from elsewhere, which links must be made for it to count?

sentinel.sentence: the portfolio a question's segment family belongs to

oral.status: taken down 2026-10-08 (s1), in Richard's words; each row names the kind it is a mutant of — ONT-005's seed
oral.theme: Richard: "a lot of the mistakes were about query efficacy … that mistake gets repeated until you have a DB of patchwork solutions and duplicate data." The mutant that produces the patchwork is a question not asked before real data existed; every row below was fine on day one.

rows.mistake: making a string field when it should have been a relation, to make product categories
rows.why: a fixed list typed as free text; when categories need details or ordering it is a 'belongs-to' to a category record

rows.mistake: designing appointment systems with on and off days, breaks, public holidays all taken into consideration when showing the available time slots, and keeping it free of race conditions
rows.why: a booking is a person on a slot at a time; without a unique-pair rule in time two people land on one slot — the availability calendar is the question 'what can it be on, and when'

rows.mistake: piling all the profile fields directly into the user table thinking there's only a few, when later the profiles needed a dozen fields and some users only use half of them
rows.why: extra detail folded into the thing it extends

rows.mistake: making relation fields where the parent record has dozens of relations, and later needing a nested query of relation objects to find the right parent — the query falls apart
rows.why: a list on the parent that nobody can query from the other side

rows.mistake: putting a field inside the profile table that is later used very often to filter users and should have been in the user table from the start; too late once users have profile relations, so a nested relation query, and it sucks
rows.why: the field you filter or sort the main thing by was split off into the extension

rows.mistake: making a one-to-many thinking 'this user only belongs to one company', then realising they can belong to several — but the field exists and real data is in it
rows.why: a 'belongs-to' that was an 'is-on'; the question 'could it ever be several at once' was not asked before data existed

rows.mistake: wanting to order users by the profile's last-updated date and having to choose between a nested query and a copied 'profile_updated' field on user kept in sync by hand — repeated until the DB is patchwork and duplicate data
rows.why: a derived field copied onto the parent and maintained by hand; the sort key belongs on the thing sorted, or the query goes through the path operation (ONT-004)
